answer_text:
The corpus presents mixed evidence regarding whether retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) improves the factual accuracy of LLM-generated answers. 

According to the provided answer, 8 papers (S003, S004, S007, S009, S012, S013, S014, S019) conclude that RAG improves factual accuracy. Conversely, 12 papers (S001, S002, S005, S006, S008, S010, S011, S015, S016, S017, S018, S020) conclude that RAG does not improve factual accuracy. 

The notes indicate that these are short controlled studies comparing retrieval-augmented conditions against parametric-only conditions on various benchmarks. The overall conclusion from the corpus is described as mixed or inconclusive. Additionally, an internal inconsistency is noted in S001, where the abstract states no measurable reduction in hallucination, but the results table shows a lower hallucination rate for the retrieval-augmented model (17.8%) compared to the parametric-only model (29.5%).
label: mixed
